messages:
sanjay: FYI getting an escalation from Support — multiple prod customers reporting elevated latency from us-west endpoints starting ~2026-03-14 03:00 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms; p99 spikes 1.1-1.6s. sample request ids: rq_20260314_acme_42, rq_20260314_beta_19. Raising here to triage.

opsbot: ALERT: edge.latency.us-west.p95 > 300ms (threshold 200ms) at 1780001000. Affected route: anycast edge-us-west.

katie: AcmeCorp sent repro steps: POST /v1/generate model=redwood-alpha, ~120 tokens, bursts at ~100rps. They hit TLS timeouts and slow connects.

maeve: Looking at our telemetry: connect times up. tcp_connect baseline ~50ms -> ~160ms, tls_handshake baseline ~20ms -> some flows ~240ms. App processing unchanged. This smells like network/path issue or a new POP causing cross-AZ hops.

kevin: Ran traceroute from us-west probe-3: 
```
traceroute to edge-us-west.redwood.net (34.120.10.8), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.9 ms
 2  52.8.10.1  2.1 ms
 3  13.77.100.12  15.6 ms
 4  * * *
 5  65.20.200.41  140.2 ms  <-- unexpected cross-AZ handoff
 6  34.120.10.8  145.9 ms
```
That big jump on hop 5 aligns with the 140ms add. Also seeing dig latency spikes for edge-us-west anycast name (120-300ms on some resolvers).

maeve: Packet captures from the front-line nodes: SYN/SYN-ACK fine, but clientHello -> serverHello delayed. Session resumption is flaky; some edge nodes lack session cache or ticket sync. That increases full TLS handshakes.

sanjay: Support also reports ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR intermittently. Any recent infra work on DNS weighting or POP changes?

kevin: We did a DNS weight canary at 02:45 UTC to route a slice through a new us-west POP. Autoscaling pushed weight up around 03:00 UTC. New POP might have poor upstream peering causing cross-AZ egress and the latency jump.

katie: Customers want ETA and mitigation steps. They're seeing search UX regressions.

maeve: Repro commands I'm running: 

curl -w "time_namelookup:%{time_namelookup} time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://edge-us-west.redwood.net/v1/generate

Bad sample: time_namelookup:0.205 time_connect:0.160 time_appconnect:0.410 time_total:0.900

openssl s_client -connect edge-us-west.redwood.net:443 -servername edge-us-west.redwood.net -msg -tlsextdebug
(we see full handshake ~230ms before AppData frames)

kevin: Proposed immediate actions (low risk):
- rollback DNS weight for the new POP and drain it
- reduce DNS TTL to 30s temporarily to speed resolver convergence
- bias routing toward POPs with healthy peering
- enable session ticket sharing across POPs to cut full handshakes

sanjay: Agreed. Sequence: 1) rollback DNS weight (kevin). 2) set TTL 30s (maeve/infra). 3) enable ticket sync if tails persist (kevin/infra). 4) open peering case.

kevin: Executing rollback now: 
```
# infra-dns ctl set-weight edge-us-west-newpop 0 --dry-run=false
```

maeve: Lowering DNS TTL in cdn-config; rollout should hit authoritative caches in ~60s.

opsbot: EVENT: DNS weight change applied by kevin at 1780001700

katie: Relaying to AcmeCorp on the phone now — will update in 10m.

maeve: After rollback, p95 dropped to ~160ms within ~3 minutes. p99 still has tails (~800ms) likely due to stale resolver caches and existing sessions.

sanjay: Good. Monitor for 30m. If p99 tails persist, enable session ticket sync and keep TTL low. Also open support case with peering provider and attach traces + SYN/TLS timings.

kevin: Opened peering ticket #PP-6543 with traces and pcap.

maeve: Follow-up: about 2.7% of client requests still hit the new POP due to a handful of stubborn ISP caches. Lower TTL helps but takes time; some resolvers ignore short TTLs. Long-term fix: geo-aware pre-warm + stronger failover during incremental weight moves to avoid cross-AZ routing loops.

katie: Customer update: noticed improvement after rollback; still seeing rare slow requests. They appreciated quick action. :thumbsup:

sanjay: Post-incident action items: 
- infra: tighten canary gating for DNS weight shifts and automatic rollback if latency delta > 200ms (owner: kevin)
- eng-runtime: add per-POP telemetry for TLS handshake vs resumption rates (owner: maeve)
- support: update incident runbook for DNS/POP customer comms (owner: katie)

kevin: Estimate full recovery (no p99 tails) in 3-6 hours as external caches expire. Will keep ticket PP-6543 updated.

opsbot: RESOLVE: edge.latency.us-west.p95 below threshold at 1780003400 (p95=158ms)

sanjay: Closing the loop. Keep an eye on spikes and reopen if needed. Thanks team.
